title: Topologically of finite type over a complete Tate ring: equivalent formulations and locality
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For an arrow of complete weakly admissible topological rings B to A, the lemma asserts the equivalence of four conditions -- tautness together with finite type of B/J to A/I for every weak ideal of definition, the same with a cofinal system of weak ideals of definition, tautness together with A being topologically of finite type over B, and A being isomorphic as a topological B-algebra to a quotient of a restricted power series algebra by a closed ideal -- and adds that these conditions define a local property, that is, they satisfy the three locality axioms (statement lines 6559-6580). Three of the implications are immediate from the definitions, and the substance is the implication from the cofinal-system formulation to the first one. That argument is a genuine construction: an inverse system of quotients A_n with A_{n+1} modulo the image of J_n equal to A_n and with A its limit is produced, finite generation is transferred downwards along the system, generators of the first stage are lifted to A, the universal property of the restricted power series algebra produces a continuous map to A, surjectivity of the induced maps on the quotients is obtained from a local nilpotence criterion, and the exactness of the inverse limit of the resulting short exact sequences -- using that the transition maps between the kernels are surjective -- shows that the map from the restricted power series algebra to A is surjective and open, with closed kernel (proof lines 6583-6620). The locality axioms (1) and (2) are then treated by a second, independent argument, in which the induced diagram between the quotients is shown to have etale horizontal maps and the two directions are read off from an algebra lemma and from the descent lemma for finiteness along a faithfully flat etale extension (proof lines 6622-6655). The claim is H3: the equivalence and the locality verification rest on different mechanisms, and the first of them requires an inverse-limit construction with an explicit Mittag-Leffler step.
